entries.reason: FALSE POSITIVE via closure attribution, and separately a considered exemption. The reported path is main.cmdCheck -> main.runCheck -> main.binaryInfo -> main.registeredToolCount -> tools.RegisterAll -> a tool constructor's handler closure -> atomicfile.Write: `vp check` COUNTS registered tools, it does not invoke them. The only vault write `vp check` performs is the transient, self-deleting .vp-fs-probe-* that CheckVaultFilesystem creates to test whether the filesystem accepts ':' in a filename — internal/check/vaultfs.go records the matching decision that the MCP-side vp_check stays Mutating:false for it. Gating a diagnostic against a newer vault would remove the tool an operator reaches for precisely when the surface mismatch is what they are diagnosing. Accepted.

DELIBERATE, and the path is GENUINE (main.cmdHook -> main.runHook -> hook.Run -> archive.Create -> archive.stampVault) — unlike the three entries above, this one really is a vault writer reached by a real call chain. It is exempt anyway: internal/surface/gate.go's EnforceWarnOnly is documented as "Used by `vp hook` and read-only CLI commands so an out-of-date binary can never block a capture." A capture that fail-stops is a capture that is LOST, and losing history to protect a schema is the wrong trade. Accepted.

DELIBERATE, and the decision predates this rule. internal/mcp/tools.go: "There is deliberately NO MCP startup gate — vp is MCP-primary, so the server stays up and the remediation surfaces in-band as a tool error payload." Writes are gated PER TOOL at Registry.gateIfMutating, which routes both dispatch paths through surface.EnforceFailStop. A CLI-level mutates() here would refuse to start the server outright, taking vp_bootstrap_context away exactly when an agent needs to find out what is wrong. HONEST NOTE ON THE PATH: the chain this rule reports runs main.cmdMCP -> main.serveMCP -> main.bootstrap -> tools.RegisterAll -> a tool constructor's handler closure -> atomicfile.Write. That is tool REGISTRATION, not invocation — an artifact of attributing a function literal's calls to the function that builds it. The exemption is real; this particular path is not evidence for it.

DELIBERATE, same ruling as main.cmdMCP: no MCP startup gate, per-tool gating at Registry.gateIfMutating. `vp mcp serve` is read-only unless --allow-writes, and that flag's writes are surface-gated at the tool seam. Reported through the same registration-closure path as cmdMCP, so the same honest note applies: registration is not invocation.

DELIBERATELY EXEMPT — a diagnostic must run when the funnel is what is being diagnosed. internal/check/vaultfs.go:141 creates a transient, self-deleting .vp-fs-probe-* at the VAULT ROOT with O_CREATE|O_WRONLY|O_EXCL to test whether the filesystem accepts ':' in a filename (the NTFS/exFAT case). Routing a filesystem-capability probe through the primitive whose correctness it is probing is circular. The same reasoning already keeps the MCP-side vp_check Mutating:false — see the sibling ungated-vault-writer main.cmdCheck entry. Census row 23.

DELIBERATELY EXEMPT — the other half of the probe in CheckVaultFilesystem above. internal/check/vaultfs.go:94 removes vault-root entries matching the .vp-fs-probe- prefix that are older than 5 minutes, i.e. residue from a probe whose process died before its own cleanup at :172. It removes only files this package created. Same circularity rationale. Census row 23.

REAL BYPASS — deferred to Option E Phase 2, family F2. internal/storage/memory.go:384 unlinks a vault memory file with a bare os.Remove. It holds the per-path vaultlock (:379) so it is not a locking defect, but it does not route through vaultfs.Delete, and being a PURE REMOVAL with no accompanying write it is invisible to any stamp-anchored rule by construction. Census row 6. Fix = make vaultfs.Delete reachable from storage.

REAL BYPASS — deferred to Option E Phase 2, family F2. internal/storage/tasks.go:866 unlinks the source task with os.Remove after writing the destination through lockedWrite (:863). The destination half is correctly funnelled; the removal half is not, so retire/cancel is half-covered. Census row 7. Fix = route the unlink through vaultfs.Move (which is what this operation actually is).

STRUCTURALLY EXEMPT — the lock primitive cannot take the lock. internal/vaultlock/vaultlock.go:99,107 creates <vault>/.vp-locks/<sha>.lock, which IS the advisory-lock file the whole discipline (ADR-003) is built on. Routing it through atomicfile.Write would require acquiring the lock in order to create the lock, and atomicfile does not lock anyway. Census row 20. Exempt with rationale, not deferred work.
